tool_arguments.query: CoreWeave customer concentration top customers percentage Q2 2026

trajectory.content: CoreWeave customer concentration top customers percentage Q2 2026

**CoreWeave’s Q2 2026 customer concentration remained very high, although it diversified materially from its prior dependence on Microsoft.** [[1]]

| Q2 2026 revenue concentration | Share of Q2 revenue | Approx. revenue dollars* |
|---|---:|---:|
| Customer A (largest; not named in the 10-Q) | 36% | $927 million |
| Customer B (not named) | 26% | $670 million |
| Customer C (not named) | 10% | $258 million |
| Top three combined | 72% | $1.85 billion |

*Calculated using Q2 revenue of $2.575 billion. [[2]] 

CoreWeave reported that no other customer represented at least 10% of revenue in the June quarter, meaning the remaining customer base collectively represented 28% of revenue. [[2]] 

For the first six months of 2026, Customer A represented 40% of revenue and Customer B represented 23%, or 63% combined; Q2’s lower 36% share for Customer A indicates some quarter-over-quarter diversification rather than the elimination of concentration risk. [[2]] 

Receivables were also concentrated: Customers A and B each accounted for 32% of net accounts receivable as of June 30, 2026, or 64% in total. [[2]]

**Can the largest customers be identified?** Not definitively from the Q2 2026 10-Q. [[1]] The filing uses anonymized labels—Customers A, B, and C—and explicitly cautions that the letter labels may refer to different customers in different reporting periods. [[1]] Therefore, it would be inappropriate to state that Q2 Customer A was Microsoft, OpenAI, Meta, or Jane Street. [[1]] 

The last explicitly named largest customer was **Microsoft**, which represented approximately **67% of CoreWeave’s FY2025 revenue**; the company did not attach a name to the 36% Q2 2026 largest-customer figure. [[1]] CoreWeave’s Q2 risk disclosure did identify Microsoft and OpenAI as “other significant customers,” while highlighting an approximately $6.0 billion April 2026 commitment from Jane Street. [[1]]

**Bottom line:** CoreWeave’s customer mix improved—its largest customer fell from 67% of FY2025 revenue to 36% in Q2 2026—but it is still an exceptionally concentrated AI-cloud provider, with 72% of quarterly revenue generated by three customers and 64% of receivables owed by two customers. [[1]] [[2]]

Sources:
[S3.1] CoreWeave (CRWV): 2026 Revenue Analysis, Top Customer Concentration & Exposure — https://sec-api.io/insights/coreweave-crwv-2026-revenue-analysis-top-customer-concentration-exposure

**CoreWeave remains highly concentrated in Microsoft, not OpenAI, on recognized revenue.** Microsoft accounted for approximately **67% of FY2025 revenue** ($5.131 billion), or roughly **$3.44 billion**, versus 62% in FY2024 and 35% in FY2023. [[1]] 

OpenAI was **not a ≥10% revenue customer in FY2025**: CoreWeave disclosed that no customer other than Microsoft represented 10% or more of FY2025 revenue. [[1]] 

That said, OpenAI is an exceptionally material **forward backlog/customer-credit exposure** rather than a disclosed current-revenue concentration. Its initial March 2025 agreement committed OpenAI to pay up to approximately **$11.9 billion through October 2030**, and a September 2025 order form added up to approximately **$6.5 billion through May 2031**; CoreWeave explicitly said it expected OpenAI to become a significant future customer. [[2]] 

CoreWeave subsequently described total OpenAI contract value at approximately **$22.4 billion**, including the initial agreement, a May 2025 expansion, and the September expansion. [[3]]

**Bottom line:** Microsoft is the dominant near-term P&L concentration risk—two-thirds of FY2025 sales—while OpenAI is the major medium-term concentration and counterparty risk embedded in contracted backlog and planned capacity deployment. [[4]] [[2]]

tool_arguments.query: CoreWeave FY2025 full year revenue and customer concentration Microsoft percentage

trajectory.content: CoreWeave FY2025 full year revenue and customer concentration Microsoft percentage

**CoreWeave remains highly concentrated in Microsoft, not OpenAI, on recognized revenue.** Microsoft accounted for approximately **67% of FY2025 revenue** ($5.131 billion), or roughly **$3.44 billion**, versus 62% in FY2024 and 35% in FY2023. [[1]] 

OpenAI was **not a ≥10% revenue customer in FY2025**: CoreWeave disclosed that no customer other than Microsoft represented 10% or more of FY2025 revenue. [[1]] 

That said, OpenAI is an exceptionally material **forward backlog/customer-credit exposure** rather than a disclosed current-revenue concentration. Its initial March 2025 agreement committed OpenAI to pay up to approximately **$11.9 billion through October 2030**, and a September 2025 order form added up to approximately **$6.5 billion through May 2031**; CoreWeave explicitly said it expected OpenAI to become a significant future customer. [[2]] 

CoreWeave subsequently described total OpenAI contract value at approximately **$22.4 billion**, including the initial agreement, a May 2025 expansion, and the September expansion. [[3]]

**Bottom line:** Microsoft is the dominant near-term P&L concentration risk—two-thirds of FY2025 sales—while OpenAI is the major medium-term concentration and counterparty risk embedded in contracted backlog and planned capacity deployment. [[4]] [[2]]

trajectory.content: Broadcom AI semiconductor revenue Q2 fiscal 2026 custom accelerators XPUs networking

**Broadcom’s Q2 FY2026 AI semiconductor revenue was $10.8 billion**, up **143% year over year**, driven by demand for **custom AI accelerators (XPUs)** and **AI networking**; the fiscal quarter ended **May 3, 2026**. [[1, 2]] 

This result was modestly above Broadcom’s Q1 outlook for **$10.7 billion** in Q2 AI semiconductor revenue, an outperformance of roughly **$0.1 billion (0.9%)**. [[3]] 

For context, Q2 semiconductor-solutions revenue was **$15.009 billion**, meaning AI semiconductors represented about **72.0%** of the segment; total company revenue was **$22.187 billion**, making AI semiconductor revenue approximately **48.7%** of consolidated sales. [[1, 2]] 

Broadcom guided Q3 FY2026 AI semiconductor revenue to **$16.0 billion**, implying more than **200% year-over-year growth** and roughly **48% sequential growth** from Q2. [[1]] 

The key takeaway is that Broadcom’s AI revenue category encompasses both the **custom accelerator/XPU silicon** deployed by hyperscalers and the **networking components** required to scale those accelerator clusters; the company did not disclose a Q2 revenue split between the two categories. [[1]]

tool_arguments.query: Broadcom Q1 FY2026 earnings call AI semiconductor revenue custom accelerator XPU networking breakdown

trajectory.content: Broadcom Q1 FY2026 earnings call AI semiconductor revenue custom accelerator XPU networking breakdown

**Broadcom’s “AI semiconductor revenue” is a management-reported revenue category rather than a separately reported GAAP operating segment; it refers principally to sales of (1) customer-specific AI compute accelerators—called custom AI accelerators or XPUs—and (2) AI networking products.** [[1]] [[2]]

**XPU** is Broadcom management’s umbrella term for the purpose-built computing accelerators it supplies for customers’ AI data centers; these are customized alternatives to general-purpose GPU-based compute, exemplified in the call by shipments of Google’s Ironwood TPU and OpenAI’s Jalapeno accelerator. [[3]] [[2]]

**Custom accelerator revenue** therefore means revenue from these customer-designed or customer-tailored AI chips, while **AI networking revenue** encompasses the high-bandwidth interconnect needed to link AI accelerators—particularly Ethernet switching and optical interconnect products. [[2]] [[3]] 

For fiscal Q3 2026, ended August 2, 2026, Broadcom reported **$16.7 billion** of AI semiconductor revenue, up **221% year over year** and **54% sequentially**. [[1]] 

Management said XPU shipments increased by more than **3.5× year over year** and represented **73%** of Q3 AI revenue, while AI-networking revenue rose more than **2.5× year over year**. [[2]] 

This AI category was the principal growth driver within Broadcom’s Semiconductor Solutions segment, whose Q3 revenue was **$20.839 billion**, up **127% year over year**; total company revenue was **$29.591 billion**. [[1]] 

For fiscal Q4 2026, Broadcom guided to **$21.7 billion** of AI semiconductor revenue, implying **236% year-over-year growth**, and management’s Q3-call outlook was approximately **$58 billion** of AI revenue for full-year fiscal 2026. [[1]] [[3]] 

In short, the phrase should be read as Broadcom’s combined AI-chip platform revenue—**custom XPU/ASIC compute plus the Ethernet/optical fabric that scales those systems**—not as revenue from a single standalone “AI semiconductor” product or a formal reported segment. [[1]] [[3]] [[2]]

tool_arguments.query: CoreWeave top customer concentration percentage Q2 2026

trajectory.content: CoreWeave top customer concentration percentage Q2 2026

**CoreWeave’s Q2 2026 customer concentration remained very high, although it diversified materially from its prior dependence on Microsoft.** [[1]]

| Q2 2026 revenue concentration | Share of Q2 revenue | Approx. revenue dollars* |
|---|---:|---:|
| Customer A (largest; not named in the 10-Q) | 36% | $927 million |
| Customer B (not named) | 26% | $670 million |
| Customer C (not named) | 10% | $258 million |
| Top three combined | 72% | $1.85 billion |

*Calculated using Q2 revenue of $2.575 billion. [[2]] 

CoreWeave reported that no other customer represented at least 10% of revenue in the June quarter, meaning the remaining customer base collectively represented 28% of revenue. [[2]] 

For the first six months of 2026, Customer A represented 40% of revenue and Customer B represented 23%, or 63% combined; Q2’s lower 36% share for Customer A indicates some quarter-over-quarter diversification rather than the elimination of concentration risk. [[2]] 

Receivables were also concentrated: Customers A and B each accounted for 32% of net accounts receivable as of June 30, 2026, or 64% in total. [[2]]

**Can the largest customers be identified?** Not definitively from the Q2 2026 10-Q. [[1]] The filing uses anonymized labels—Customers A, B, and C—and explicitly cautions that the letter labels may refer to different customers in different reporting periods. [[1]] Therefore, it would be inappropriate to state that Q2 Customer A was Microsoft, OpenAI, Meta, or Jane Street. [[1]] 

The last explicitly named largest customer was **Microsoft**, which represented approximately **67% of CoreWeave’s FY2025 revenue**; the company did not attach a name to the 36% Q2 2026 largest-customer figure. [[1]] CoreWeave’s Q2 risk disclosure did identify Microsoft and OpenAI as “other significant customers,” while highlighting an approximately $6.0 billion April 2026 commitment from Jane Street. [[1]]

**Bottom line:** CoreWeave’s customer mix improved—its largest customer fell from 67% of FY2025 revenue to 36% in Q2 2026—but it is still an exceptionally concentrated AI-cloud provider, with 72% of quarterly revenue generated by three customers and 64% of receivables owed by two customers. [[1]] [[2]]

tool_arguments.query: CoreWeave top customer concentration percentage revenue FY2025

trajectory.content: CoreWeave top customer concentration percentage revenue FY2025

**CoreWeave remains highly concentrated in Microsoft, not OpenAI, on recognized revenue.** Microsoft accounted for approximately **67% of FY2025 revenue** ($5.131 billion), or roughly **$3.44 billion**, versus 62% in FY2024 and 35% in FY2023. [[1]] 

OpenAI was **not a ≥10% revenue customer in FY2025**: CoreWeave disclosed that no customer other than Microsoft represented 10% or more of FY2025 revenue. [[1]] 

That said, OpenAI is an exceptionally material **forward backlog/customer-credit exposure** rather than a disclosed current-revenue concentration. Its initial March 2025 agreement committed OpenAI to pay up to approximately **$11.9 billion through October 2030**, and a September 2025 order form added up to approximately **$6.5 billion through May 2031**; CoreWeave explicitly said it expected OpenAI to become a significant future customer. [[2]] 

CoreWeave subsequently described total OpenAI contract value at approximately **$22.4 billion**, including the initial agreement, a May 2025 expansion, and the September expansion. [[3]]

**Bottom line:** Microsoft is the dominant near-term P&L concentration risk—two-thirds of FY2025 sales—while OpenAI is the major medium-term concentration and counterparty risk embedded in contracted backlog and planned capacity deployment. [[4]] [[2]]

tool_arguments.query: Broadcom AI semiconductor revenue Q3 fiscal 2026 custom AI accelerators XPUs

trajectory.content: Broadcom AI semiconductor revenue Q3 fiscal 2026 custom AI accelerators XPUs

Broadcom reported **$16.7 billion of AI-semiconductor revenue in fiscal Q3 2026**, ended **August 2, 2026**, up **221% year over year** and **54% sequentially**. [[1]] 

Management attributed the acceleration to very strong demand for **custom AI accelerators (XPUs)** and AI networking; total company revenue was **$29.6 billion**, so AI semiconductors represented roughly **56%** of quarterly revenue. [[1]] [[2]] 

The XPU product cycle included high-volume delivery of Google’s **Ironwood TPU v7** to Google and Anthropic, while Broadcom also identified custom XPU programs for OpenAI (“Jalapeño”) and Meta (MTIA). [[3]] 

For fiscal Q4 2026, Broadcom guided AI-semiconductor revenue to **$21.7 billion**, or **236% year-over-year growth**, implying continued sharp expansion in custom accelerators and networking. [[1]]

trajectory.content: Broadcom custom AI accelerator XPU revenue breakdown fiscal Q3 2026

Broadcom’s fiscal Q3 2026—ended August 2, 2026—AI semiconductor revenue was **$16.7 billion**, up **221% year over year** and **54% sequentially**. [[1]]

| Q3 FY2026 AI-semiconductor revenue breakdown | Share of AI revenue | Revenue |
|---|---:|---:|
| Custom AI accelerators / XPUs | 73% | **~$12.2bn** |
| AI networking—including Ethernet switching and optical interconnects | 27% | **~$4.5bn** |
| **Total AI semiconductor revenue** | **100%** | **$16.7bn** |

Broadcom said XPU shipment volume increased by **more than 3.5x year over year** and constituted **73%** of AI revenue; AI-networking revenue increased by **more than 2.5x year over year**. [[2]] 

On this basis, XPU revenue represented roughly **41.2%** of Broadcom’s total Q3 consolidated revenue of **$29.6 billion**. [[1]] [[2]]

tool_arguments.query: Broadcom fiscal year end November 2025 2026 annual report AI semiconductor revenue

trajectory.content: Broadcom fiscal year end November 2025 2026 annual report AI semiconductor revenue

Broadcom’s fiscal 2025 ended **November 2, 2025**—not at the end of November—because its fiscal year ends on the Sunday closest to October 31. [[1]] 

For FY2025, Broadcom reported **$20.0 billion of AI semiconductor revenue**, up **65% year over year**, according to CEO Hock Tan’s year-end earnings-call remarks. [[2]] 

That AI revenue was generated principally from **custom AI accelerators (XPUs) and AI networking**, while Broadcom’s reported Semiconductor Solutions segment revenue was **$36.858 billion**, up 22% year over year. [[1]] [[3]] 

Thus, AI semiconductor revenue represented approximately **54.3%** of FY2025 Semiconductor Solutions revenue ($20.0bn ÷ $36.858bn). [[2]] [[1]] 

For context, Broadcom reported total FY2025 revenue of **$63.887 billion**, including **$36.858 billion** in Semiconductor Solutions and **$27.029 billion** in Infrastructure Software. [[1]] 

There is **no FY2026 annual report yet** as of October 17, 2026: Broadcom had reported through fiscal Q3 ended August 2, 2026, and guided Q4 to end November 1, 2026. [[4]] 

Based on reported FY2026 quarterly AI semiconductor revenue of **$8.4 billion in Q1**, **$10.8 billion in Q2**, and **$16.7 billion in Q3**, plus the company’s **$21.7 billion Q4 forecast**, FY2026 AI semiconductor revenue would total approximately **$57.6 billion if Q4 guidance is achieved**; this is an estimate, not an annual-report result. [[5]] [[6]] [[4]]

**CoreWeave remains highly concentrated in Microsoft, not OpenAI, on recognized revenue.** Microsoft accounted for approximately **67% of FY2025 revenue** ($5.131 billion), or roughly **$3.44 billion**, versus 62% in FY2024 and 35% in FY2023. [[1]] 

OpenAI was **not a ≥10% revenue customer in FY2025**: CoreWeave disclosed that no customer other than Microsoft represented 10% or more of FY2025 revenue. [[1]] 

That said, OpenAI is an exceptionally material **forward backlog/customer-credit exposure** rather than a disclosed current-revenue concentration. Its initial March 2025 agreement committed OpenAI to pay up to approximately **$11.9 billion through October 2030**, and a September 2025 order form added up to approximately **$6.5 billion through May 2031**; CoreWeave explicitly said it expected OpenAI to become a significant future customer. [[2]] 

CoreWeave subsequently described total OpenAI contract value at approximately **$22.4 billion**, including the initial agreement, a May 2025 expansion, and the September expansion. [[3]]

**Bottom line:** Microsoft is the dominant near-term P&L concentration risk—two-thirds of FY2025 sales—while OpenAI is the major medium-term concentration and counterparty risk embedded in contracted backlog and planned capacity deployment. [[4]] [[2]]

trajectory.content: CoreWeave customer concentration top 5 customers revenue percentage Q2 2026

**CoreWeave’s Q2 2026 customer concentration remained very high, although it diversified materially from its prior dependence on Microsoft.** [[1]]

| Q2 2026 revenue concentration | Share of Q2 revenue | Approx. revenue dollars* |
|---|---:|---:|
| Customer A (largest; not named in the 10-Q) | 36% | $927 million |
| Customer B (not named) | 26% | $670 million |
| Customer C (not named) | 10% | $258 million |
| Top three combined | 72% | $1.85 billion |

*Calculated using Q2 revenue of $2.575 billion. [[2]] 

CoreWeave reported that no other customer represented at least 10% of revenue in the June quarter, meaning the remaining customer base collectively represented 28% of revenue. [[2]] 

For the first six months of 2026, Customer A represented 40% of revenue and Customer B represented 23%, or 63% combined; Q2’s lower 36% share for Customer A indicates some quarter-over-quarter diversification rather than the elimination of concentration risk. [[2]] 

Receivables were also concentrated: Customers A and B each accounted for 32% of net accounts receivable as of June 30, 2026, or 64% in total. [[2]]

**Can the largest customers be identified?** Not definitively from the Q2 2026 10-Q. [[1]] The filing uses anonymized labels—Customers A, B, and C—and explicitly cautions that the letter labels may refer to different customers in different reporting periods. [[1]] Therefore, it would be inappropriate to state that Q2 Customer A was Microsoft, OpenAI, Meta, or Jane Street. [[1]] 

The last explicitly named largest customer was **Microsoft**, which represented approximately **67% of CoreWeave’s FY2025 revenue**; the company did not attach a name to the 36% Q2 2026 largest-customer figure. [[1]] CoreWeave’s Q2 risk disclosure did identify Microsoft and OpenAI as “other significant customers,” while highlighting an approximately $6.0 billion April 2026 commitment from Jane Street. [[1]]

**Bottom line:** CoreWeave’s customer mix improved—its largest customer fell from 67% of FY2025 revenue to 36% in Q2 2026—but it is still an exceptionally concentrated AI-cloud provider, with 72% of quarterly revenue generated by three customers and 64% of receivables owed by two customers. [[1]] [[2]]

Broadcom guided Q3 FY2026 AI semiconductor revenue to **$16.0 billion**, implying more than **200% year-over-year growth** and roughly **48% sequential growth** from Q2. [[1]] 

The key takeaway is that Broadcom’s AI revenue category encompasses both the **custom accelerator/XPU silicon** deployed by hyperscalers and the **networking components** required to scale those accelerator clusters; the company did not disclose a Q2 revenue split between the two categories. [[1]]

tool_arguments.query: CoreWeave top customers concentration largest AI cloud providers Q2 2026

trajectory.content: CoreWeave top customers concentration largest AI cloud providers Q2 2026

**CoreWeave’s Q2 2026 customer concentration remained very high, although it diversified materially from its prior dependence on Microsoft.** [[1]]

| Q2 2026 revenue concentration | Share of Q2 revenue | Approx. revenue dollars* |
|---|---:|---:|
| Customer A (largest; not named in the 10-Q) | 36% | $927 million |
| Customer B (not named) | 26% | $670 million |
| Customer C (not named) | 10% | $258 million |
| Top three combined | 72% | $1.85 billion |

*Calculated using Q2 revenue of $2.575 billion. [[2]] 

CoreWeave reported that no other customer represented at least 10% of revenue in the June quarter, meaning the remaining customer base collectively represented 28% of revenue. [[2]] 

For the first six months of 2026, Customer A represented 40% of revenue and Customer B represented 23%, or 63% combined; Q2’s lower 36% share for Customer A indicates some quarter-over-quarter diversification rather than the elimination of concentration risk. [[2]] 

Receivables were also concentrated: Customers A and B each accounted for 32% of net accounts receivable as of June 30, 2026, or 64% in total. [[2]]

**Can the largest customers be identified?** Not definitively from the Q2 2026 10-Q. [[1]] The filing uses anonymized labels—Customers A, B, and C—and explicitly cautions that the letter labels may refer to different customers in different reporting periods. [[1]] Therefore, it would be inappropriate to state that Q2 Customer A was Microsoft, OpenAI, Meta, or Jane Street. [[1]] 

The last explicitly named largest customer was **Microsoft**, which represented approximately **67% of CoreWeave’s FY2025 revenue**; the company did not attach a name to the 36% Q2 2026 largest-customer figure. [[1]] CoreWeave’s Q2 risk disclosure did identify Microsoft and OpenAI as “other significant customers,” while highlighting an approximately $6.0 billion April 2026 commitment from Jane Street. [[1]]

**Bottom line:** CoreWeave’s customer mix improved—its largest customer fell from 67% of FY2025 revenue to 36% in Q2 2026—but it is still an exceptionally concentrated AI-cloud provider, with 72% of quarterly revenue generated by three customers and 64% of receivables owed by two customers. [[1]] [[2]]

**CoreWeave’s Q2 2026 customer concentration remained very high, although it diversified materially from its prior dependence on Microsoft.** [[1]]

| Q2 2026 revenue concentration | Share of Q2 revenue | Approx. revenue dollars* |
|---|---:|---:|
| Customer A (largest; not named in the 10-Q) | 36% | $927 million |
| Customer B (not named) | 26% | $670 million |
| Customer C (not named) | 10% | $258 million |
| Top three combined | 72% | $1.85 billion |

*Calculated using Q2 revenue of $2.575 billion. [[2]] 

CoreWeave reported that no other customer represented at least 10% of revenue in the June quarter, meaning the remaining customer base collectively represented 28% of revenue. [[2]] 

For the first six months of 2026, Customer A represented 40% of revenue and Customer B represented 23%, or 63% combined; Q2’s lower 36% share for Customer A indicates some quarter-over-quarter diversification rather than the elimination of concentration risk. [[2]] 

Receivables were also concentrated: Customers A and B each accounted for 32% of net accounts receivable as of June 30, 2026, or 64% in total. [[2]]

**Can the largest customers be identified?** Not definitively from the Q2 2026 10-Q. [[1]] The filing uses anonymized labels—Customers A, B, and C—and explicitly cautions that the letter labels may refer to different customers in different reporting periods. [[1]] Therefore, it would be inappropriate to state that Q2 Customer A was Microsoft, OpenAI, Meta, or Jane Street. [[1]] 

The last explicitly named largest customer was **Microsoft**, which represented approximately **67% of CoreWeave’s FY2025 revenue**; the company did not attach a name to the 36% Q2 2026 largest-customer figure. [[1]] CoreWeave’s Q2 risk disclosure did identify Microsoft and OpenAI as “other significant customers,” while highlighting an approximately $6.0 billion April 2026 commitment from Jane Street. [[1]]

**Bottom line:** CoreWeave’s customer mix improved—its largest customer fell from 67% of FY2025 revenue to 36% in Q2 2026—but it is still an exceptionally concentrated AI-cloud provider, with 72% of quarterly revenue generated by three customers and 64% of receivables owed by two customers. [[1]] [[2]]

tool_arguments.query: Broadcom definition AI semiconductor revenue custom accelerator XPU networking fiscal 2026 earnings call

trajectory.content: Broadcom definition AI semiconductor revenue custom accelerator XPU networking fiscal 2026 earnings call

**Broadcom’s “AI semiconductor revenue” is a management-reported revenue category rather than a separately reported GAAP operating segment; it refers principally to sales of (1) customer-specific AI compute accelerators—called custom AI accelerators or XPUs—and (2) AI networking products.** [[1]] [[2]]

**XPU** is Broadcom management’s umbrella term for the purpose-built computing accelerators it supplies for customers’ AI data centers; these are customized alternatives to general-purpose GPU-based compute, exemplified in the call by shipments of Google’s Ironwood TPU and OpenAI’s Jalapeno accelerator. [[3]] [[2]]

**Custom accelerator revenue** therefore means revenue from these customer-designed or customer-tailored AI chips, while **AI networking revenue** encompasses the high-bandwidth interconnect needed to link AI accelerators—particularly Ethernet switching and optical interconnect products. [[2]] [[3]] 

For fiscal Q3 2026, ended August 2, 2026, Broadcom reported **$16.7 billion** of AI semiconductor revenue, up **221% year over year** and **54% sequentially**. [[1]] 

Management said XPU shipments increased by more than **3.5× year over year** and represented **73%** of Q3 AI revenue, while AI-networking revenue rose more than **2.5× year over year**. [[2]] 

This AI category was the principal growth driver within Broadcom’s Semiconductor Solutions segment, whose Q3 revenue was **$20.839 billion**, up **127% year over year**; total company revenue was **$29.591 billion**. [[1]] 

For fiscal Q4 2026, Broadcom guided to **$21.7 billion** of AI semiconductor revenue, implying **236% year-over-year growth**, and management’s Q3-call outlook was approximately **$58 billion** of AI revenue for full-year fiscal 2026. [[1]] [[3]] 

In short, the phrase should be read as Broadcom’s combined AI-chip platform revenue—**custom XPU/ASIC compute plus the Ethernet/optical fabric that scales those systems**—not as revenue from a single standalone “AI semiconductor” product or a formal reported segment. [[1]] [[3]] [[2]]

trajectory.content: Broadcom AI networking revenue Q3 fiscal 2026 custom accelerators XPUs breakdown

Broadcom reported **$16.7 billion of AI-semiconductor revenue in fiscal Q3 2026**, ended **August 2, 2026**, up **221% year over year** and **54% sequentially**. [[1]] 

Management attributed the acceleration to very strong demand for **custom AI accelerators (XPUs)** and AI networking; total company revenue was **$29.6 billion**, so AI semiconductors represented roughly **56%** of quarterly revenue. [[1]] [[2]] 

The XPU product cycle included high-volume delivery of Google’s **Ironwood TPU v7** to Google and Anthropic, while Broadcom also identified custom XPU programs for OpenAI (“Jalapeño”) and Meta (MTIA). [[3]] 

For fiscal Q4 2026, Broadcom guided AI-semiconductor revenue to **$21.7 billion**, or **236% year-over-year growth**, implying continued sharp expansion in custom accelerators and networking. [[1]]

trajectory.content: Broadcom definition AI semiconductor revenue custom accelerator XPU networking fiscal 2026 earnings call

**Broadcom’s “AI semiconductor revenue” is a management-reported revenue category rather than a separately reported GAAP operating segment; it refers principally to sales of (1) customer-specific AI compute accelerators—called custom AI accelerators or XPUs—and (2) AI networking products.** [[1]] [[2]]

**XPU** is Broadcom management’s umbrella term for the purpose-built computing accelerators it supplies for customers’ AI data centers; these are customized alternatives to general-purpose GPU-based compute, exemplified in the call by shipments of Google’s Ironwood TPU and OpenAI’s Jalapeno accelerator. [[3]] [[2]]

**Custom accelerator revenue** therefore means revenue from these customer-designed or customer-tailored AI chips, while **AI networking revenue** encompasses the high-bandwidth interconnect needed to link AI accelerators—particularly Ethernet switching and optical interconnect products. [[2]] [[3]] 

For fiscal Q3 2026, ended August 2, 2026, Broadcom reported **$16.7 billion** of AI semiconductor revenue, up **221% year over year** and **54% sequentially**. [[1]] 

Management said XPU shipments increased by more than **3.5× year over year** and represented **73%** of Q3 AI revenue, while AI-networking revenue rose more than **2.5× year over year**. [[2]] 

This AI category was the principal growth driver within Broadcom’s Semiconductor Solutions segment, whose Q3 revenue was **$20.839 billion**, up **127% year over year**; total company revenue was **$29.591 billion**. [[1]] 

For fiscal Q4 2026, Broadcom guided to **$21.7 billion** of AI semiconductor revenue, implying **236% year-over-year growth**, and management’s Q3-call outlook was approximately **$58 billion** of AI revenue for full-year fiscal 2026. [[1]] [[3]] 

In short, the phrase should be read as Broadcom’s combined AI-chip platform revenue—**custom XPU/ASIC compute plus the Ethernet/optical fabric that scales those systems**—not as revenue from a single standalone “AI semiconductor” product or a formal reported segment. [[1]] [[3]] [[2]]

tool_arguments.query: Broadcom wireless chips Apple revenue fiscal Q3 2026 quarterly shipment units

trajectory.content: Broadcom wireless chips Apple revenue fiscal Q3 2026 quarterly shipment units

Broadcom reported **$16.7 billion of AI-semiconductor revenue in fiscal Q3 2026**, ended **August 2, 2026**, up **221% year over year** and **54% sequentially**. [[1]] 

Management attributed the acceleration to very strong demand for **custom AI accelerators (XPUs)** and AI networking; total company revenue was **$29.6 billion**, so AI semiconductors represented roughly **56%** of quarterly revenue. [[1]] [[2]] 

The XPU product cycle included high-volume delivery of Google’s **Ironwood TPU v7** to Google and Anthropic, while Broadcom also identified custom XPU programs for OpenAI (“Jalapeño”) and Meta (MTIA). [[3]] 

For fiscal Q4 2026, Broadcom guided AI-semiconductor revenue to **$21.7 billion**, or **236% year-over-year growth**, implying continued sharp expansion in custom accelerators and networking. [[1]]

Related coverage:
Apple’s disclosed Broadcom wireless-components contract is a **multiyear, multibillion-dollar** agreement announced on May 23, 2023; Broadcom is to develop 5G RF components, including FBAR filters, plus other wireless-connectivity components, with FBAR design and production in U.S. facilities including Fort Collins, Colorado. [[1]] 

Neither Apple nor Broadcom publicly disclosed a contract value or a standalone “wireless chip revenue” figure. [[1]] Broadcom did disclose that aggregate sales to Apple through all channels represented approximately **20% of total revenue in FY2023**, while FY2023 revenue was **$35.819 billion**; that implies roughly **$7.16 billion** of total Broadcom revenue attributable to Apple, but this is an estimate across Broadcom products and channels—not revenue attributable solely to the wireless agreement. [[2]] [[3]] 

For context, Broadcom’s wireless business is seasonally sensitive to new mobile-device launches, so Apple-related RF and connectivity revenue can be meaningfully weighted toward the second half of Broadcom’s fiscal year. [[4]]

**Broadcom’s Q2 FY2026 AI semiconductor revenue was $10.8 billion**, up **143% year over year**, driven by demand for **custom AI accelerators (XPUs)** and **AI networking**; the fiscal quarter ended **May 3, 2026**. [[1, 2]] 

This result was modestly above Broadcom’s Q1 outlook for **$10.7 billion** in Q2 AI semiconductor revenue, an outperformance of roughly **$0.1 billion (0.9%)**. [[3]] 

For context, Q2 semiconductor-solutions revenue was **$15.009 billion**, meaning AI semiconductors represented about **72.0%** of the segment; total company revenue was **$22.187 billion**, making AI semiconductor revenue approximately **48.7%** of consolidated sales. [[1, 2]] 

Broadcom guided Q3 FY2026 AI semiconductor revenue to **$16.0 billion**, implying more than **200% year-over-year growth** and roughly **48% sequential growth** from Q2. [[1]] 

The key takeaway is that Broadcom’s AI revenue category encompasses both the **custom accelerator/XPU silicon** deployed by hyperscalers and the **networking components** required to scale those accelerator clusters; the company did not disclose a Q2 revenue split between the two categories. [[1]]

Broadcom reported **$16.7 billion of AI-semiconductor revenue in fiscal Q3 2026**, ended **August 2, 2026**, up **221% year over year** and **54% sequentially**. [[1]] 

Management attributed the acceleration to very strong demand for **custom AI accelerators (XPUs)** and AI networking; total company revenue was **$29.6 billion**, so AI semiconductors represented roughly **56%** of quarterly revenue. [[1]] [[2]] 

The XPU product cycle included high-volume delivery of Google’s **Ironwood TPU v7** to Google and Anthropic, while Broadcom also identified custom XPU programs for OpenAI (“Jalapeño”) and Meta (MTIA). [[3]] 

For fiscal Q4 2026, Broadcom guided AI-semiconductor revenue to **$21.7 billion**, or **236% year-over-year growth**, implying continued sharp expansion in custom accelerators and networking. [[1]]

Sources:
[S8.1] Broadcom Inc. Announces Third Quarter Fiscal Year 2026 Financial Results and Quarterly Dividend — https://investors.broadcom.com/news-releases/news-release-details/broadcom-inc-announces-third-quarter-fiscal-year-2026-financial

tool_arguments.query: CoreWeave top 5 customer revenue concentration percentage FY 2025

trajectory.content: CoreWeave top 5 customer revenue concentration percentage FY 2025

**CoreWeave remains highly concentrated in Microsoft, not OpenAI, on recognized revenue.** Microsoft accounted for approximately **67% of FY2025 revenue** ($5.131 billion), or roughly **$3.44 billion**, versus 62% in FY2024 and 35% in FY2023. [[1]] 

OpenAI was **not a ≥10% revenue customer in FY2025**: CoreWeave disclosed that no customer other than Microsoft represented 10% or more of FY2025 revenue. [[1]] 

That said, OpenAI is an exceptionally material **forward backlog/customer-credit exposure** rather than a disclosed current-revenue concentration. Its initial March 2025 agreement committed OpenAI to pay up to approximately **$11.9 billion through October 2030**, and a September 2025 order form added up to approximately **$6.5 billion through May 2031**; CoreWeave explicitly said it expected OpenAI to become a significant future customer. [[2]] 

CoreWeave subsequently described total OpenAI contract value at approximately **$22.4 billion**, including the initial agreement, a May 2025 expansion, and the September expansion. [[3]]

**Bottom line:** Microsoft is the dominant near-term P&L concentration risk—two-thirds of FY2025 sales—while OpenAI is the major medium-term concentration and counterparty risk embedded in contracted backlog and planned capacity deployment. [[4]] [[2]]
